# Unified Sparse-Dense Decoder Retrieval with Learned Query Routing

## Core Problem

Can a single decoder-only LLM produce both high-quality SPLADE-style sparse and dense bi-encoder representations through jointly trained dual output heads, with a lightweight learned router that adaptively weights their contributions per query, without degrading either modality compared to single-task baselines?

## Research Opportunity

Three verified gaps converge to create a timely opening: (1) no decoder-only LLM produces both sparse and dense representations from a single forward pass with learned heads — LACONIC-8B (Jan 2026) and Lion-SP/DS (SIGIR 2025) train separate models while BGE-M3 unifies but only on encoder-only XLM-RoBERTa; (2) no learned per-query router exists within a unified retrieval model — RouterRetriever (AAAI 2025) routes between separate external models, DAT requires LLM inference per query, and BGE-M3 uses fixed interpolation weights; (3) bidirectional self-distillation between sparse and dense heads has never been validated in decoder-only architectures — the CIKM 2025 proof uses VLP encoder models (BLIP/ALBEF). All required building blocks are now individually proven: LACONIC's two-phase curricu...

## Research Landscape

Current SOTA on MTEB Retrieval is led by Gemini Embedding 2 (67.71 nDCG@10, proprietary) and NV-Embed-v2 (62.65, open-weight, dense-only with latent attention pooling on Mistral-7B). For sparse retrieval, LACONIC-8B achieves 60.2 MTEB-R and 61.5 BEIR-14 average using Llama-3-8B with a two-phase curriculum, while CSplade-bi-8B reaches 55.3 BEIR with a 6.7 GB index (vs 135 GB dense). The Lion-SP/DS study (SIGIR 2025) quantified that sparse outperforms dense by 10.5% on BEIR at 8B scale (55.2 vs 50.1 nDCG@10), confirming strong complementarity. BGE-M3 remains the only unified sparse+dense model but is limited to encoder-only XLM-RoBERTa with fixed-weight interpolation (s_rank = w₁·s_dense + w₂·s_lex + w₃·s_mul). RouterRetriever demonstrated +2.1 NDCG@10 from learned routing across domain-specific LoRA experts, but operates between separate models. Key limitations: no single decoder-only model combines both modalities; fixed interpolation ignores per-query variation in optimal sparse-vs-de...

## Proposed Approach

Fine-tune Llama-3.1-8B with bidirectional attention, adding dual heads over shared backbone: sparse SPLADE head (vocab projection + ReLU + FLOPS reg) and dense head (latent attention pooling). Three-stage curriculum: (1) sparse-only adaptation (10k steps, CSplade protocol), (2) joint contrastive training with bidirectional self-KD between heads using CIKM 2025 formula, (3) hard-negative fine-tuning with learned 2-layer MLP router predicting per-query sparse-dense interpolation weights.

## Detailed Description

Hydra-Retrieve is a unified decoder-only retrieval model producing both sparse and dense representations from one forward pass via jointly trained dual output heads with a learned per-query router. Built on Llama-3.1-8B with bidirectional attention, it adds a sparse SPLADE head (vocab projection + ReLU + FLOPS regularization) and a dense latent-attention-pooling head sharing all transformer layers. A three-stage curriculum trains the system: (1) sparse adaptation stabilizing ReLU activations following CSplade, (2) joint contrastive learning with bidirectional self-KD where each head's scores serve as soft teacher signal for the other, extending the CIKM 2025 formula to decoder-only text retrieval, and (3) hard-negative tuning with a learned MLP router predicting per-query interpolation weights. No concurrent work combining all three innovations was found in arXiv or OpenReview through May 2026. We target >61 nDCG@10 on MTEB Retrieval and >62 on BEIR-14, surpassing LACONIC-8B (60.2) and Lion-SP-8B (55.2) while enabling adaptive fusion at zero extra inference cost.

## Key References

- LACONIC: Dense-Level Effectiveness for Scalable Sparse Retrieval (arXiv 2026)
- CSPLADE: Learned Sparse Retrieval with Causal Language Models (IJCNLP 2025)
- M3-Embedding: Multi-Linguality Multi-Functionality Multi-Granularity (ACL Findings 2024)
- RouterRetriever: Routing over a Mixture of Expert Embedding Models (AAAI 2025)
- NV-Embed: Improved Techniques for Training LLMs as Generalist Embedding Models (ICLR 2025)

## LACONIC-8B Model

LACONIC is a family of learned sparse retrievers based on the Llama3 architecture (1B, 3B, and 8B), using a streamlined two-phase training curriculum consisting of weakly supervised pre-finetuning to adapt causal LLMs for bidirectional contextualization and high-signal finetuning using curated hard negatives.

LACONIC-8B achieves an impressive average 60.2 nDCG@10 on 15 MTEB Retrieval datasets, ranked 15th on the leaderboard as of January 1, 2026, being the only learned sparse retrieval model at this position. The 8B variant achieves state-of-the-art 60.2 nDCG on the MTEB Retrieval benchmark while utilizing 71% less index memory than an equivalent dense model.

## Related Work: Scaling Sparse and Dense Retrieval

Another relevant study on decoder-only LLMs examines scaling behavior. Using MSMARCO passages as the training dataset, decoder-only LLMs (Llama-3 series: 1B, 3B, 8B), and a fixed compute budget, researchers evaluated various training configurations on both in-domain (MSMARCO, TREC DL) and out-of-domain (BEIR) benchmarks.

Sparse retrieval models consistently outperform dense retrieval across both in-domain and out-of-domain benchmarks with greater robustness to imperfect supervised signals, and sparse retrieval models with the combination of CL and KD losses at 8B scale achieved state-of-the-art results in all evaluation sets.

## Overview

BGE-M3 stands for Multi-linguality (100+ languages), Multi-granularities (input length up to 8192), Multi-Functionality (unification of dense, lexical, multi-vec/colbert retrieval).

## Unified Sparse-Dense Design

BGE-M3 trains a single model to support dense retrieval, sparse retrieval, and multi-vector (ColBERT-style) retrieval simultaneously, using self-knowledge distillation to align the three output heads. Self-knowledge distillation combines multiple outputs from different retrieval modes as reward signal to enhance the performance of single mode (especially for sparse retrieval and multi-vec/colbert retrieval).

The model performs ablation studies by removing the long document data from the fine-tuning stage, and after this modification, the dense method can still outperform the majority of baselines, which indicates that its empirical advantage has been well established during the pre-training stage.

## Evaluation on Benchmarks

BGE-M3 was evaluated on multiple retrieval benchmarks including MIRACL (Multilingual ad-hoc retrieval in 18 languages) using nDCG@10 as the primary metric. The model shows strong performance across BEIR and MTEB evaluations, with the combination of all three retrieval modes (dense + sparse + multi-vector) yielding the best results.

## RouterRetriever Overview

RouterRetriever is a retrieval model that leverages a mixture of domain-specific experts by using a routing mechanism to select the most appropriate expert for each query. It is lightweight and allows easy addition or removal of experts without additional training.

## Experimental Results and Baselines

Evaluation on the BEIR benchmark demonstrates that RouterRetriever outperforms both models trained on MSMARCO (+2.1 absolute nDCG@10) and multi-task models (+3.2). This is achieved by employing a routing mechanism which surpasses other routing techniques (+1.8 on average) commonly used in language modeling.

## Ablation Study and Oracle Analysis

RouterRetriever consistently outperforms single model baselines (MSMARCO and Multi-Task) in terms of nDCG@10 on BEIR benchmark, surpasses various standard routing techniques commonly used in language modeling, achieves performance comparable to the DatasetOracle model, and the InstanceOracle indicates room for future work in router improvements.

## Key Finding

RouterRetriever is the first work to demonstrate the advantages of routing over a mixture of domain-specific expert embedding models as an alternative to a single, general-purpose embedding model, especially when retrieving from diverse, specialized domains.

## Overview
CSplade is a learned sparse retrieval method with causal language models by Xu, Feng, Tian, Ding, and Cheong, published at IJCNLP-AACL 2025 in Mumbai, India.

## Methodology
Sparse retrieval represents documents with vocabulary-sized vectors where most elements are zeros, which can subsequently be used in an inverted index for efficient retrieval. The approach addresses the limitations of traditional sparse retrieval by leveraging pre-trained language models to mitigate the weakness of methods that focus on capturing lexical match signals.

## Training Details

Based on my search results, here are the key findings about SPLADE training instability, regularization issues, and solutions in 2025:

## Training Instability with LLM-Based SPLADE

Recent research has identified two challenges in training large language models for learned sparse retrieval: (1) training instability during the early stage of contrastive training; (2) suboptimal performance due to pre-trained LLM's unidirectional attention. This is addressed in the CSPLADE variant that uses causal language models.

## FLOPS Regularization Issues

SPLADE uses FLOPS regularization to encourage vector sparsity during training, however FLOPS regularization does not ensure sparsity among terms—only within a given query or document. Terms with very high Document Frequencies substantially increase latency, which is a practical issue for deployment.

## Alternative Solution: DF-FLOPS Regularization

To address FLOPS limitations, DF-FLOPS addresses this by enforcing sparsity over both documents and terms. DF-FLOPS regularization penalizes activation of high document-frequency terms rather than global density, with a dynamic weighting scheme that discourages common trivial terms, decreasing posting list lengths and end-to-end retrieval latency, while retaining salient high-DF terms if justified by context.

## Recent 2025 Approaches

Joint regularization (jFLOPS) and batchwise mask control enhance alignment between query and document sparsity, improving practical search overheads. Additionally, Echo-Mistral-SPLADE utilizes a causal decoder-only LLM backbone with echo embeddings for sparse expansion, surpassing all previous SPLADE variants.
